build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

extra: tile set 0, unpacked from T35/L12 by enter_map ($2722) with map 0

comments.text: Tile 0 of tile set 0 (the world map's): blank, all 32 bitmap bytes zero, so its square shows the black background; the same in all nine sets. Map 0 has no square of tile 0 in its tile layer and draws 27 off its edge, not 0; on other maps tile 0 is the off-map tile when record byte $33 is 0, and the encounter figure of monster kind 0 ($5BF5 = 0).

Tiles 1-6, figures that are the same in all nine sets: 1 a grey and white robot-like humanoid with a flat disc for a head, 2 a hulking red and orange figure with one white eye, 3 a thin yellow and green figure running, 4 a brown-haired man in a cyan shirt and blue trousers, 5 a white and grey tied sack, 6 a brown horned creature. The game's encounter scan draws 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 on an encounter square in view (game $95FA: tile = $5BF5 + byte 6 of the monster's record, the table holding 0 6 3 4 2 1; tile 4 when the monster type has bit 7 set); draw_square shows 5 on every loot-bag square (class 5, $0B99). The world map has none of them in its tile layer and no encounter or loot-bag squares.

Tile 7, a brown-haired figure in a green shirt and brown trousers, the same in all nine sets: the party. The game draws it on the party's square after every view redraw (game $AF1D-$AF25: LDA #$07, JMP draw_tile), and a class-4 square whose record byte 1 is 7 shows it too; the world map's layer and class-4 records do not use it. Map 0's swap_tiles ($4FCD) exchanges tile 7's bitmap and colour bytes with tile 86's, the jeep at (29, 41), when the jeep is fixed (class-6 record 4, $4D83), and swaps them back at (26, 31) (class-6 record 5, $4D88), so the party is drawn as the jeep on the drive between. draw_tile's LDA $D0E0,X ($2367) has its operand rewritten for each tile ($22F0-$2307) and points here because tile 7 was the last tile drawn.

Tile 8, a yellow disc with three black blades (a radiation sign), the same in all nine sets: draw_square shows it instead of the layer's tile on class-9 (radiation) squares while the hour $0E is 18-23 or 0-5 ($0B80-$0B8A). The world map has 36 such squares (x 53-62, y 34-40), showing their ground tile by day; none of its tile layer holds 8.

Tile 9 of set 0: white strokes with purple, red and blue, a purple and white arch over white bars striped blue and red (set 6 has the same picture; sets 1-5, 7 and 8 a purple peak over blue bars). The game draws tile 9 on the square of every other party that stands on the current map within the view (game $AD13-$AD49, from bytes +8 x, +9 y and +10 map of each party's table). Not in the world map's tile layer.

Tiles 10-15 of the world set. 11-14 are building icons, the towns and places of map 0: 29 squares, 27 of them class 10 (exits into other maps). 11 an orange block with a white step (4 squares), 12 a tall blue block (9, among them (55, 62), where the party stands outside the Ranger Center in play-map), 13 a blue block over blue and white stripes (8; one is class 1, and (59, 7) is class 4, which draw_square shows as tile 32), 14 two orange blocks striped white (8). 10, blank, and 15, solid white (every pixel pair 11, colour RAM), are unused by the map.

Tiles 16-32, the world map's open ground: short dashes on black, red in 16, 18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 29 and 31, green in 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 28, 30 and 32; 24 is blank and unused by the map. 25-32 cover most of map 0 (474, 296, 473, 427, 391, 283, 543 and 464 squares in order), 17-23 less (68, 2, 64, 5, 60, 10, 62), 16 one square. The red tiles but 25 lie on class-6 or class-11 squares. 27 is also drawn off the map's edge (record byte $33), and 32 on the two class-4 squares.

Tiles 33-45, single landmarks of the world map: 33 three light green shapes under a white bar (one square, (43, 46), class 10), 35 a white frame filled with green stripes ((35, 55), class 1), 36 and 37 a thin blue line across green ground (36 at (46, 59) and (48, 59), 37 at (49, 59)), 38 a white hut under a brown roof ((32, 52), class 10), 42 a white striped oval edged in blue on green ground ((2, 3), a class-4 square that draw_square shows as tile 32). 43, a variant of the oval, is in no layer but is the tile of map 0's class-4 record 2 ($4D50, byte 1 $AB: tile 43, blocking), which module 4's after_the_blast ($CBD5-$CBDC) puts on (2, 3). Unused by the map: 34 and 44 blank, 39 a white house front, 40 and 41 green pine trees, 45 black with two red dots.

Tiles 46-59, dark grey mountains with white snowy edges on the green speckled ground: peaks, slopes and ridge ends, 222 squares of the world map (46: 28, 47: 12, 48: 15, 49: 26, 50: 29, 51: 19, 52: 28, 53: 24, 54: 10, 55: 7, 56: 2, 57: 6, 58: 8, 59: 8), every one a class-11 square, the class that blocks the encounter scan's line of sight (game $8347).

Tiles 60-63: 60 and 62 blue water speckled light blue, 61 solid green, 63 solid red. Only 62 is in the world map's layer, on 78 squares of the lake and the river, all class 2; 60, 61 and 63 are unused by the map.

Tiles 64-69, the same dark grey mountains with white edges on red speckled ground: 49 squares of the world map (64: 8, 65: 14, 66: 6, 67: 9, 68: 9, 69: 3), class 11 but for one square each of 66 and 68 (class 12).
Tiles 70-72, unused by the world map: 70 blank, 71 a corner of white bars, 72 two east-west white bars, both edged in red and blue like 87-95.

Tiles 73-76, the diagonal banks of the river and the lake: blue water speckled light blue against the green ground along a diagonal, one tile per corner (73: 6, 74: 10, 75: 23, 76: 19 squares of the world map, all class 2). 75's colour bytes are all $E6, so the corner beyond its white edge shows light blue specks on black, not green ground.

Tiles 77-86, the river: blue water between white banks. 79 (7 squares) and 84 (the same bitmap, unused) run north-south, 80 (6) east-west; 77 (6), 78 (4) and 82 (3) have notched banks where it bends; 81 is a grey and white bridge across it (3 squares, (58, 3), (27, 31) and (27, 50), class 1). 83 and 85 are blank and unused; 86, a white rounded frame with two green panels, stands alone at (29, 41) on a class-2 square, check square 0 ('You see a broken down jeep.'): the jeep. Once Ace fixes it the square becomes class 6 number 4 ($4D83), whose map code (swap_tiles $4FCD) exchanges 86's bitmap and colour bytes with the party's tile 7 for the drive to (26, 31), where class-6 record 5 ($4D88) swaps them back.

Tiles 87-95, white bars edged in red and blue, none in the world map's layer: 87 and 88 north-south runs, 89 and 90 junctions, 91 two east-west runs, 92 and 93 north-south bars that stop halfway down, 94 and 95 short east-west stubs.

Colour bytes of tiles 0-9, four a tile, one a cell (high nibble: pixel pairs 01, low nibble: pairs 10): 0 $26; 1 $CF grey and light grey; 2 $28 red and orange; 3 $57 green and yellow; 4 $39 over $36, cyan shirt, brown hair, blue trousers; 5 $B7 then $BC, dark grey and grey (the cell with $B7 has no pixel pair 10, so its yellow never shows); 6 $98 brown and orange; 7 $59 green and brown; 8 $76, yellow (its bitmap has no pixel pair 10, so the blue nibble never shows); 9 $46 then $26 in set 0. Tiles 0-8 have these bytes in all nine sets.

Colour bytes of tiles 10-15: $98 (brown, orange) for the orange icons 11 and 14, $E6 (light blue, blue) for 12 and 13, with $C6 (grey, blue) in 13's top right cell; $26 for the blank 10 and the solid white 15, whose pixel pairs 11 all take colour RAM's white.

Colour bytes of the world map's ground, tiles 16-32: $26 (red for pairs 01) for the red speckles, $55 or $56 (green) for the green ones; 26 has $25 in its left cells, 20 $2D (light green for pairs 10) in its bottom left cell.

Colour bytes of the landmarks, tiles 33-45: $D5 (light green, green) for 33; $56 for the tiles on green ground, 35-37, 42 and 43; $99, $59, $59, $56 for the hut 38 (brown roof); $26 over $56 for the house front 39; $55 for the pines 40 and 41; $26 for 34, 44 and 45.
Colour bytes of the green mountains, tiles 46-59: $5B (green dashes, dark grey rock) in cells with rock, $56 or $55 in cells of plain ground.
Colour bytes of tiles 60-63: $E6 (light blue speckles, blue water) for 60 and 62, $56 for the solid green 61, $26 for the solid red 63.
Colour bytes of the red mountains, tiles 64-69: $2B (red dashes, dark grey rock) in rock cells, $26 in cells of plain red ground.
Colour bytes of tiles 70-72, all $26: red for pixel pairs 01 and blue for 10 around the white bars, which come from colour RAM.
Colour bytes of the lake shore, tiles 73-76: $E6 in the water cells and $56 (green, blue) in one cell each of 73 (bottom left), 74 (top right) and 76 (bottom right); 75 is $E6 throughout.

Colour bytes of the river, tiles 77-86: $26 (blue water, red marks on the banks) for most cells, $C6 (grey, blue) in 77's bottom left cell, 78's left cells and the whole bridge 81; $56 and $52 (green, blue, red) for 86.
Colour bytes of the white bars, tiles 87-95, all $26, the same byte as the unused blank tiles of this set.
